fact: The Ministry of ICT and Innovation's published ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2024/25-2028/29 is presented as a plan the Ministry and its affiliated agencies are committed to implement, with no draft status stated; dated by its cover 1 January 2025 (document date used).
The plan is a PDF on the Ministry of ICT and Innovation's own site (minict.gov.rw).
The plan covers FY2024/25 to 2028/29 (document date used).

The contents list an Implementation Plan (section 4.1, Appendix II) and Cost and Financing with budget allocation across priority areas (section 5); only the contents are in the excerpt, so no figures are given (document date used).
The plan commits the Ministry of ICT and Innovation and its affiliated agencies to deliver its programmes and initiatives (document date used).
The New Times, 28 September 2026, refers to Rwanda's ICT Sector Strategic Plan as an existing plan that emphasises aligning education outcomes with industry demand.

KT Press says Rwanda is implementing its ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029; no event date is given, so the document's published date is used.

fact: The joint ICT sector review lists the ICT Sector Strategic Plan as covering 2018-2024; no date for the stated period is given, so the review's publication date 2023-10-26 is used.

The ICT Sector Working Group's backward-looking review for 2022/23 has a section on progress against 2022/23 targets, NST1, the SSP and SDGs, and a section on lessons learned from NST1 and SSP implementation; the retained passages give no figures, so the review's publication date 2023-10-26 is used.

The INCLUDE report says the government developed the ICT Sector Strategic Plan (2018-2024) towards a digital-enabled economy through integrated e-governance platforms; no event date is given, so the report's publication date 2022-09 is used.

The Ministry of ICT and Innovation convened the sector review on 22 November 2024 with the stated objective of validating the ICT Sector Strategic Plan aligned to NST2, including its Theory of Change, M&E matrix and Implementation Plan, and the document presents the plan's outcomes as discussed.
MINICT convened the ICT Sector Working Group review of the sector plan under the guidance of MINECOFIN, which the document presents as the body overseeing implementation and monitoring.

The document sets out the plan's goal, priority areas and outcomes with listed actions and numeric targets (for example 1.5 million citizens trained in coding and ICT skills, 50,000 digital jobs) and an Implementation Plan to be validated, but states no costs and gives no dates for the actions.

The review reports FY2023/24 progress against NST1/SSP targets on some objectives, for example digitised public services at 91% against the NST1 target of 100% by 2024 and youth digital literacy at 86.8% against a target of 100%, but not on every objective.
